guide.name: Atlanta Weekends from Dahlonega to Savannah
guide.description: Six weekend trips from Atlanta, from the North Georgia mountains and Athens to Chattanooga, Highlands and Savannah, each with a place to stay, two places to eat and a few things to do.

properties.name: Hall House Hotel
properties.notes: A small hotel in an 1880s building right on the town square, so everything in Dahlonega is a short walk. Rooms are upstairs over the shops and restaurants.

properties.name: Amicalola Falls Lodge
properties.notes: The state park lodge sits on the mountain above the falls, about half an hour west of Dahlonega. Walk out the door to the trails and the long view toward Atlanta.
properties.address: 418 Amicalola Falls Lodge Road, Dawsonville, GA 30534

properties.name: Back Porch Oyster Bar
properties.notes: Oysters, shrimp and seafood pastas a few steps off the square. Ask for the porch when the weather is good.

properties.name: Montaluce Winery & Restaurant
properties.notes: A Tuscan-style winery a few miles outside town with a tasting room and a restaurant overlooking the vines. Book ahead for weekend brunch or dinner.

properties.name: Dahlonega Gold Museum State Historic Site
properties.notes: The 1836 courthouse in the middle of the square tells the story of the 1829 gold rush and the branch mint that once struck coins in town.

properties.name: Amicalola Falls State Park
properties.notes: One of the tallest waterfalls in the Southeast, with a staircase climb beside it and an approach trail to the start of the Appalachian Trail. Parking fees apply; check the official site.
properties.address: 418 Amicalola Falls Lodge Road, Dawsonville, GA 30534

properties.name: Rivet House
properties.notes: A boutique hotel in a converted factory building at the old Southern Mill complex, northwest of downtown, with an Italian restaurant and a small spa on site. Downtown is a short drive or ride-share away.

properties.name: Five & Ten
properties.notes: A long-running Athens dinner spot in a house on Milledge Avenue, cooking Southern food with local farm produce. Save it for a Saturday night and reserve ahead.

properties.name: The National
properties.notes: A downtown neighborhood restaurant with Mediterranean-leaning plates, a good bar and a patio. Easy for lunch between walks around campus.

properties.name: State Botanical Garden of Georgia
properties.notes: The university's garden south of town, with a glass conservatory, themed gardens and miles of wooded trails along the Middle Oconee River.

properties.name: Georgia Museum of Art
properties.notes: The official state art museum, on the university's east campus, with a strong collection of American paintings and decorative arts from the South.

properties.name: Blue Ridge Inn Bed & Breakfast
properties.notes: An 1890 Victorian house a block from downtown, with a wraparound porch and a cooked breakfast. A good alternative to renting a cabin up a mountain road.
properties.address: 477 W First St, Blue Ridge, GA 30513

properties.name: Harvest on Main
properties.notes: A Main Street dinner and lunch spot built around local sourcing: grass-fed beef from nearby farms, seasonal vegetables and North Georgia trout, with a long wine list.
properties.address: 576 E Main St, Blue Ridge, GA 30513

properties.name: Black Sheep Restaurant
properties.notes: Dinner and weekend brunch in an old house with a big covered patio and outdoor bar under the oaks.
properties.address: 480 W Main St, Blue Ridge, GA 30513

properties.name: Blue Ridge Scenic Railway
properties.notes: A train from the downtown depot along the Toccoa River to McCaysville, where you can step across the Tennessee line before riding back. Book ahead for fall color weekends.

properties.name: Mercier Orchards
properties.notes: A family orchard north of town with a big market, a bakery known for fried pies, hard cider and pick-your-own seasons for berries and apples.
properties.address: 8660 Blue Ridge Dr, Blue Ridge, GA 30513

properties.name: Toccoa River Swinging Bridge
properties.notes: A long suspension footbridge over the Toccoa on the Benton MacKaye Trail, a short walk from a gravel forest road lot. The road is rough, so higher clearance helps.
properties.address: Forest Service Road 816, off Aska Road, Blue Ridge, GA 30513

properties.name: The Read House
properties.notes: Chattanooga's grand 1920s hotel downtown, restored with a dark-wood lobby bar and a steakhouse. Walkable to the Southside and a short ride to the river.
properties.address: 107 W M L King Blvd, Chattanooga, TN 37402

properties.name: The Dwell Hotel
properties.notes: A small hotel in an early 1900s building downtown, with each room decorated differently and a bright solarium cafe downstairs.

properties.name: Main Street Meats
properties.notes: A Southside butcher shop with a restaurant attached, known for its burger, house charcuterie and steaks cut in-house.

properties.name: St. John's Restaurant
properties.notes: Chattanooga's longtime special-occasion dinner, cooking regional American food with local ingredients. It has moved downtown to Chestnut Street, so ignore older listings on Market Street.

properties.name: Tennessee Aquarium
properties.notes: Two buildings on the riverfront: one follows a raindrop from the Appalachian headwaters down the Tennessee River, the other covers the oceans. Give it half a day.

properties.name: Walnut Street Bridge
properties.notes: An 1890s truss bridge now open only to people on foot and bikes, linking downtown with the North Shore's shops and Coolidge Park. Best at sunset.
properties.address: Walnut St & Riverfront Pkwy, Chattanooga, TN 37402

properties.name: Rock City Gardens
properties.notes: The old roadside attraction on top of Lookout Mountain, just over the Georgia line: a path through sandstone formations, a swinging bridge and Lover's Leap with its view across several states.

properties.name: Old Edwards Inn and Spa
properties.notes: The splurge stay in Highlands, a restored 1870s inn on Main Street with a full spa and rooms spread across several buildings in town.

properties.name: Highlander Mountain House
properties.notes: A relaxed, more affordable stay on Main Street styled like an English country house, with fires in the common rooms, a pet-friendly bunkhouse out back and a tavern for dinner.

properties.name: Madison's Restaurant
properties.notes: The dining room off the Old Edwards lobby, cooking with produce from the inn's own farm. Worth a dinner even if you stay elsewhere; reserve ahead.

properties.name: Mountain Fresh Grocery
properties.notes: A grocery, deli, bakery and coffee bar where you can grab breakfast or build a trail lunch before heading out to the overlooks.

properties.name: Whiteside Mountain Trail
properties.notes: A two-mile loop to the top of sheer granite cliffs, with long views over the Chattooga valley. There is a small parking fee at the trailhead.

properties.name: Dry Falls
properties.notes: A short paved path and stairs lead behind a waterfall in the Cullasaja Gorge, so you can stand under the overhang and stay mostly dry. Check the Forest Service site for closures.

properties.name: The Marshall House
properties.notes: An 1850s hotel on Broughton Street with iron balconies, a central location between the river and the squares, and plenty of ghost stories.

properties.name: The Thunderbird Inn
properties.notes: A 1960s motor inn redone in retro colors at the west edge of the historic district. The budget pick, with parking and an easy walk to City Market.

properties.name: Mrs. Wilkes' Dining Room
properties.notes: Weekday lunch served family-style at shared tables, bowls of fried chicken and Southern sides passed around with strangers. Expect a line, bring cash, and note the winter break.

properties.name: The Grey
properties.notes: A restored 1938 Greyhound bus station where the kitchen cooks Southern food through a Savannah port-city lens. Reserve well ahead for dinner.
properties.address: 109 Martin Luther King Jr Blvd, Savannah, GA 31401

properties.name: Forsyth Park
properties.notes: The big green at the south end of the historic district, with its fountain, live oaks and a Saturday farmers market. Walk up through the squares to get there.
properties.address: Gaston St & Whitaker St, Savannah, GA 31401

properties.name: Bonaventure Cemetery
properties.notes: A Victorian cemetery on a bluff over the Wilmington River, with moss-draped oaks and carved monuments. Pick up a map at the gate and go early in the day.

properties.name: Wormsloe State Historic Site
properties.notes: A long avenue of live oaks leads to the tabby ruins of an 18th-century colonial estate, with marsh trails and a small museum.
